candidates.title: Coca-Cola's unified global identity ('one seamless visual identity') leaves Zero Sugar looking almost identical to Original; confusion three months on
candidates.claim: Official: system across 200+ markets; principle 'recognizable at a glance'; Rapha Abreu: 'with one seamless visual identity, we can deliver one recognizable brand experience'; Zero Sugar cues = larger 'Zero Sugar' text, black Dynamic Ribbon on cans, black cap on PET. Creative Bloq (2026-10-11): confusion persists; Original and Zero hard to tell apart at a glance. Attack of the Fanboy (2026-10-07): Melbourne flight attendant TikTok 'Lost count of how many wrong Cokes I've handed out this week'; cues visible only after rotating the can. Packaging Europe (2026-07-27): experts split; Ryan Selvy: uniform red 'becomes an accessibility issue'. Agency JKR (Creative Bloq 2026-07-20).
candidates.note: Official page + 4 independent pages read. Confusion evidence is anecdotal/social (one TikTok, expert comments); no sales data. Say 'reports/complaints', never 'sales fell'. Rollout list on official page includes the Middle East; never name the region's countries in copy.

candidates.title: Coca-Cola 2011 white polar-bear cans confused with silver Diet Coke; replaced by red within weeks (precedent)
candidates.claim: 1.4bn white cans announced 25 Oct 2011 (WWF polar bear partnership); shoppers said they looked like silver Diet Coke and bought the wrong one; by 2 Dec only a red version was shipping. Coca-Cola did not explicitly cite confusion; it issued a fact sheet of differences.
candidates.note: Use as precedent only: 'same lesson, 15 years earlier'. Do not say Coca-Cola admitted the reason.

candidates.title: Pollfish survey: 74% found new Coke packaging appealing; 87% unaware; 35% linked the script to Marlboro
candidates.claim: n=400 US adults online; 74% appealing; 87% unaware of the update; 28% said identical to current packaging; 35% attributed isolated script to Marlboro.
candidates.note: Vendor-run, US, small sample; supporting colour only. Marlboro angle is a tobacco association; avoid in copy.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C01 is solid on what Coca-Cola did and said (official page). Weak spot: evidence of harm is anecdotal (one TikTok, expert quotes, Creative Bloq commentary); no sales or complaint statistics. Copy must say 'people report / complaints', not 'it failed'. The 2011 precedent is documented, but Coca-Cola never officially attributed the switch to confusion. Do not repeat the Reddit 'kill regular Coke' theory or the Marlboro joke. Pollfish is a vendor survey (n=400, US).
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Universal, instantly felt moment: grabbing the wrong can. Shoppers scan, they don't read (System 1); colour is the fastest cue. Tension flips a belief marketers hold sacred: consistency is always good. Persian business owners with product lines (cosmetics, food, dairy, tea) face exactly this when they 'unify' packaging.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Pure brand strategy (brand architecture, packaging systems): Behnood's core. Practical close: one sign for the brand, one unmistakable cue for each product, tested at arm's length in one second. Works equally in fa and en; global brand, no local politics.
lenses_summary.overlap_check: Adjacent to 2026-10-24 (recognition) but the inverse problem: there the redesign erased the brand; here the brand is so consistent it erases the product. Do not reuse Tropicana or Ehrenberg-Bass material.

story.tension: Consistency makes the brand recognisable; too much of it makes the product unfindable.
story.concrete_image: Two red cans side by side; the one you wanted is the other one.
story.runner_up: C07 Klarna 'we don't have fans' (strong line, no image)

decision.why: Highest total (89), strongest tension and most concrete image; works for both audiences; verifiable core facts from the official release.
